title: Not just pools. Not just summer.
lede: As little as an inch or two of water is enough, and it doesn’t wait for swim season. Our mom, Shannon, says it in four words: “Drowning has no season.” Any water a little one can reach needs a layer of protection.

places.title: The bathtub
places.text: Most child drownings inside the home happen in the bathtub, usually during a quick break in supervision. For babies under 1, it’s the most common place of all.
places.tip: Stay within arm’s reach until bath time is over. If you have to step away, even for a second, take the baby with you.

places.title: An inch or two of water
places.text: Buckets, toilets, coolers of melted ice, kiddie pools and the puddle on top of a pool cover. A toddler can drown in as little as an inch or two of water.
places.tip: Empty buckets, coolers and kiddie pools right after you use them, and put latches on toilet lids.

places.title: While the house is asleep
places.text: Kids wake up early, sleepwalk and wander. Among people with autism, deaths are nearly 40 times as likely to be caused by drowning as deaths in the general population.
places.tip: Keep doors to the water locked and alarmed at night too, latch the pool gate every time, and make a wandering plan if your child has autism.

places.title: In winter clothes
places.text: Kids who fall in aren’t dressed to swim. Jeans, boots and a heavy coat soak up water fast, and water colder than 70°F can make anyone gasp and lose control of their breathing.
places.tip: Self-rescue lessons like ISR have kids practice floating in their clothes and shoes, because that’s how it really happens.

places.title: Off-season water
places.text: Pool drownings peak in summer, but bathtubs, hot tubs, ponds and covered pools don’t take the winter off. Rain and snowmelt collect on pool covers, and a child can drown in less than 2 inches of water.
places.tip: Keep the fence and gate locked all year, use a certified safety cover and pump the water off it, and keep kids off the ice.

places.title: On the busiest days
places.text: Holidays, birthday parties, a house full of company. Adam slipped out during graduation week, with family in from out of town and nobody expecting him anywhere near the pool.
places.tip: Name a Water Watcher any time kids and water are together, and check that doors, gates and alarms are still set when the company leaves.

quote: A party, a nearby bucket, a bathtub, a pond, the bayou, a door without an alarm and a breathtaking pool without a 4 sided fence.
